summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude all military retirement pay, retainer pay, and related disability or combat compensation from gross income for federal tax purposes, effective for tax years after enactment.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the tax code to exclude military retirement benefits from gross income. This is a revenue-side change that does not alter any federal spending programs, appropriations, or outlays. It has no direct or indirect effect on government spending levels.

The core provision rewrites IRC Section 122 to fully exclude retired or retainer pay and certain disability/compensation amounts for members of the Armed Forces from federal income tax. This constitutes a direct and substantial tax reduction targeted at veterans and uniformed services retirees.

The bill contains no provisions related to health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, hospitals, or medical care delivery. The limited reference to disability compensation is incidental and does not alter healthcare policy.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, restrictions, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to visas, border security, asylum, or immigration enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive health services, funding restrictions, or abortion access.

While the bill benefits military retirees through tax relief, it does not change defense appropriations, troop levels, procurement, or any spending authorized under titles 10 or 37. The tax treatment of retirement pay is separate from defense budget authority.
No environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions appear in the bill.
The bill affects tax treatment of military retirement, not means-tested welfare programs such as SNAP, TANF, or SSI.
No provisions concern schools, student aid, or education funding.
No provisions relate to controlled substances, enforcement, or decriminalization.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal procedure.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.

By reducing taxable income for a class of recipients, the bill will decrease federal revenue and thereby increase the deficit relative to current law. This moves away from prioritizing debt reduction.
No provisions address nondiscrimination, marriage, or legal protections based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
No provisions address foreign assistance, State Department funding, or international programs.
No provisions address voting rights, election administration, or campaign finance.
No provisions address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance.
No provisions address collective bargaining, union rights, or workplace regulations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, conscience protections, or civil rights enforcement.
